findings.title: Daylight, Night, and Stilling
findings.claim: The prohibition against rebuking the asker also protects a disclosed need from being forced out of cover into public exposure.
findings.mechanism: The focus form retains the ordinary rebuke reading while its supplied daylight branch meets 93:1 and the night-and-stilling branches meet 93:2. That ordered contrast makes harsh response legible as coercive exposure, so non-rebuke preserves cover as well as dignity.
findings.reader_payoff: The command reaches beyond severe tone: a need brought forward under cover should not be made more exposed by the answer.
findings.containment: The focus verb is not being redefined as daylight or night. The privacy edge is a bounded pericope resonance; the same light-and-night sequence can also remain a reassurance contrast without this implication.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies exact focus/context anchors, branch glosses or facets, and citable channel support for this bounded pericope relation.
